svg.text: Front coil-spring pocket - section through the spring axis (x = 34.5), 12 mm magazine
Body grey, slider tan, spring to scale (4.0 mm OD, 0.4 mm wire, 20 mm free, 12 active coils), M3 screw dark red. Body front wall at the left; the slider travels left-right. 1 mm grid.
Dashed grey = body bore axis. The bow drawn in the BEFORE panels is an illustration of the failure, not a measurement; everything else is the real sectioned geometry.
EXTENDED - slider fully forward, spring at its longest. THIS IS THE CASE THAT MATTERS.

g.text: 9.95 mm in open air - nothing stops it bowing
both bores d4.4, nothing inside the spring
bores d4.6, M3 x 16 hex BUTTON HEAD threaded into the body wall

svg.text: COMPRESSED - slider hard against its back stop.

g.text: near coil bind at this length; owner reports it is never reached
both bores d4.4, nothing inside the spring
near coil bind at this length; owner reports it is never reached
bores d4.6, M3 x 16 hex BUTTON HEAD threaded into the body wall

svg.text: The same spring at its 20 mm FREE length, to the same scale - it never reaches it, so the slider is always pushed:
slider fully forward 15.95 mm (4.05 mm preload, about 1.8 N)
slider at the back stop 6.05 mm
M3 x 16 hex-socket BUTTON HEAD (ISO 7380), self-tapped into a d2.5 hole, 1.40 mm engagement, head buried in a d6.0 counterbore 0.66 mm below the face - nothing proud to catch on the rail.
